fields.label: Skill Name (slug)
fields.description: Stable identifier (kebab-case). Used as the doctype 'name' and in /skills toggle commands. Example: 'ar-collections'.

fields.label: Title
fields.description: Human-friendly name shown in the chat-ui Skills palette.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: One-paragraph summary of what this skill does. Surfaced in the chat-ui under the title.

fields.label: System Prompt Snippet
fields.description: Appended to the base system prompt when this skill is active. Tells the LLM how to behave inside this skill (focus, tone, decision rules, examples).

fields.label: Allowed Tools (JSON array)
fields.description: Optional. JSON array of tool names. When set, the agent's tools/list response is filtered to this subset for the active conversation, so the LLM physically cannot use anything else. Leave empty to allow all 38 tools. Example: ["get_outstanding", "prepare_send_email"]

fields.label: Examples (markdown)
fields.description: Optional sample interactions shown in the skill's detail view. Plain markdown.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: When unchecked, the skill is hidden from the Skills palette.

fields.label: Public (visible to all users)
fields.description: When checked, every authenticated user sees this skill in the palette. Otherwise only the owner does. System Manager only.

fields.options:
A Skill packages a focused agent persona — a system prompt + an optional restricted tool subset + examples — that the user can activate from the chat-ui's / palette.

When active, the skill's system prompt appends to the base prompt, and (if allowed_tools is set) the LLM only sees that subset for the rest of the conversation. Multiple skills can stack.

Examples
  • AR Collections — receivables follow-up; tools restricted to outstanding + email + comment.
  • Item Onboarding — guides the user through creating Items with the right defaults.

Both are seeded as is_public = 1 on install. Add your own via New Lazychat Skill.
